backward_compat_traps.normal_control: 1 byte; sequence numbers mod-8; max 7 outstanding I-frames.
backward_compat_traps.extended_control: 2 bytes; sequence numbers mod-128; max 127 outstanding I-frames.
backward_compat_traps.trap: Normal and extended control field widths are NOT auto-negotiable on-the-fly — they are selected by the mode-set command (SNRM vs SNRME, SABM vs SABME, etc.). Mismatched assumption causes immediate decode failure.
FCS size MUST be agreed at link setup (typically via XID); a 32-bit FCS sender to a 16-bit FCS receiver will produce gibberish at the data-link layer.

backward_compat_traps.sync_bit_stuffing: 0-bit inserted after 5 consecutive 1-bits in frame body.
backward_compat_traps.async_octet_stuffing: 0x7E and 0x7D in payload are escaped with 0x7D + (octet XOR 0x20).
backward_compat_traps.trap: PPP-async and PPP-sync both use HDLC framing but with different stuffing rules; a PPP-async-only receiver cannot decode a synchronous bit-stuffed HDLC stream and vice-versa.

backward_compat_traps.shared_allowed: Spec allows the 0-bit at the end of a closing flag to be SHARED with the start-of-next-flag: bits '011111101111110' (15 bits, not 16).
backward_compat_traps.trap: Some hardware does not support shared-flag receive and gets confused on back-to-back frames; spec text explicitly notes this incompatibility.

backward_compat_traps.sdlc_specific: SDLC defined NR0..NR3 (Nonreserved), CFGR (Configure), BCN (Beacon), AC0/AC1 — these are NOT part of ISO/IEC 13239 HDLC.
backward_compat_traps.trap: An SDLC frame on an HDLC-only receiver will decode the U-frame M-bits as 'unknown' and trigger FRMR with W flag set.

fields.spec_version: ISO/IEC 13239:2002 (High-Level Data Link Control procedures — consolidated edition)
previous_versions: IBM SDLC (1975) — Synchronous Data Link Control, layer 2 protocol for IBM SNA. Predecessor of HDLC.
ISO 3309-1979 — Frame Structure (original HDLC frame layout).
ISO 4335-1979 — Elements of Procedure (frame types, sequence numbers, mode-set commands).
ISO 6159-1980 — Unbalanced Classes of Procedure (NRM, ARM).
ITU-T X.25 LAPB (1976+) — extended HDLC for X.25 packet-switched networks.
ANSI ADCCP (1979) — essentially identical to HDLC; ANSI's parallel standardization.
IEEE 802.2 LLC (1985) — adopted HDLC frame structure for LANs.
PPP framing (RFC 1662, 1994) — HDLC-like framing for serial PPP.
V.42 LAPM (1988) — modem error correction; HDLC-derived.

key_changes.summary: Generalized IBM SDLC into a vendor-neutral ISO standard; same frame structure; broader U-frame command set.
Codified NRM/ARM (unbalanced primary-secondary) and ABM (balanced peer-to-peer) as separate classes.

Replaced ISO 3309 + 4335 + 6159 + 6256 with a single revised standard. Added: SM (generic Set Mode) with parameter information field, UIH (UI with header check), 15-bit and 31-bit extended sequence numbers (selected only via SM command).
Cisco's proprietary variant: adds a 2-byte protocol-type field after the standard Control field to identify the upper-layer protocol (similar to PPP's PPP-protocol field).

PPP adopts HDLC-like framing but always uses Address=0xFF (all-stations) and Control=0x03 (UI command, no sequence numbers); upper-layer PPP-protocol field follows. Asynchronous PPP uses octet stuffing.

fields.version_naming_history_note: Bosch-style: there is no single 'manufacturer' for HDLC. ISO/IEC 13239:2002 is the current authoritative reference. PPP framing (RFC 1662) inherits HDLC frame structure but specifies its own elements of procedure (no sequence numbers, fixed Address+Control). LAPB (X.25), LAPD (ISDN Q.921), LAPF (Frame Relay Q.922), LAPM (V.42) are all HDLC variants with bespoke option sets.
